title: Project-naming advice is answered before optional implementation

source.note: The user asks how to name imported projects from the git repository name. The assistant recommends a naming rule, then offers to implement it and asks for config only for a separate reuse diagnosis.

messages.text: a. i feel like we should be able to resume a containerized session onto a compatible raw checkout, how should we make that work? b. are containerized sesions always bundle even w/ just one root? if so, should probably special-case that
2. yes but resume-into-existing-worktree should be allowed like new-from-worktree right?

Implementation is underway. Recap of what's happening and the plan:

**Design locked in:**
- Resume gains an optional project directory. Supplying one for a bundle-session resume onto a bare target flips the session to raw shape, then reuses the creation-time flavor rule unchanged: a primary checkout gets a managed worktree (`.hel/worktrees/<session_id>`, branch `hel/<session_id>`), a linked worktree is used in place — exactly matching "new-from-worktree".
- The restore spec gains per-repository overrides (destination, branch, `existing_checkout`) so the archived state lands in the user's checkout and the harness cwd rewrite follows it.
- In-place restores get hard pre-flight gates before anything is mutated: clean tracked tree, commit availability (`git bundle verify` / head reachable, with one fetch-origin retry), local-branch ancestry, and untracked-file collision scan.
- Two v1 restrictions: single-repository sessions only, and the selected directory must be the repo root (patches and the untracked tar are repo-root-relative).
- Two safety fixes folded in: `connect_local_repositories` must skip raw-shaped sessions (otherwise a flipped session's bundle config could rewire the user checkout's origin to the hel-local proxy), and a failed resume cleans up a worktree it created before rolling back.

An Opus agent is now implementing the restore layer and controller changes with tests (no commit — I review first). The TUI step (project-directory prompt in the resume wizard, reusing the existing new-session directory input) comes after that review, since it depends on the controller API. What landed:

- **Restore layer** (`hel_checkpoint.rs`, `hel_archive.rs`): the restore spec gains per-repository overrides — destination, branch, and an `existing_checkout` flag. Overrides are applied in one place so the git restore and the harness cwd rewrite agree on where the checkout lives. For checkouts Hel doesn't own, all pre-flight gates run before anything is mutated: clean tracked tree, checkpoint commits present (`git bundle verify` or head-commit check, with one repair fetch from origin), no diverged same-named local branch, no untracked-file collisions.
- **Controller** (`hel_controller.rs`): resume accepts an optional project directory for a bundle session on a bare target. It validates up front (single-repository checkpoint, absolute path, repository root), flips the session to raw shape, and lets provisioning apply the same flavor rule as creation — primary checkout gets a managed worktree on `hel/<session-id>`, a linked worktree is restored in place on the archived branch. The feature is complete: two commits on master, both reviewed by me and fully validated (rustfmt, clippy `-D warnings`, 791 tests passing).

**`abc918c` — Resume a container session onto a raw checkout** (restore layer + controller)
- The restore spec gains per-repository overrides: destination, branch, and an `existing_checkout` flag. One rewrite point feeds both the git restore and the harness cwd rewrite, so Claude/Kimi/Codex session state follows the checkout to its real path.
- Resume accepts an optional project directory when the archived session was a container session and the target is bare. The session flips to raw shape and provisioning applies the same flavor rule as creation: a primary checkout gets a managed worktree on `hel/<session-id>`; a linked worktree is restored in place on the archived branch — the symmetry with new-from-worktree you asked for.
- In-place restores are gated before anything is touched: clean tracked tree, checkpoint commits present (`git bundle verify` or head-commit check, one repair fetch from origin), no diverged same-named local branch, no untracked-file collisions. All gates run across the board before any mutation, so a refusal leaves the checkout untouched.
- A failed resume rolls back the flip and removes a worktree it created; an end-to-end test proves this against the real database and real git, including that the persisted target row transitions from container to `local-bare` cleanly.

**`f08d2dd` — Resume wizard checkout step** (TUI)
- Resuming a single-repository container session onto a bare target adds a checkout step: required on local-bare, optional on ssh-bare where an empty field keeps today's fresh-clone behavior. The review step shows where state will land, and validation stays on the async action round-trip (no event-loop blocking).
- Multi-repository sessions get an inline error on local-bare and keep the fresh-clone path on ssh-bare.
- The project-directory input (history, prefill, path checks, async validation) is now one shared component between the new-session and resume wizards instead of a near-duplicate.

The v1 limits we agreed on are enforced with plain error messages: single-repository sessions only, and the selected directory must be the repository root (patches and the untracked tar are repo-root-relative). Natural follow-ups if you want them later: multi-root support via a per-root directory mapping, and letting the harness cwd be a subdirectory of the restored repo. how do we auto-name projects for the dashboard

i resumed a session from raw to container and it got named `import-$projectname`, i'd prefer just $projectname [i.e. git repo name]
Now let me check the current state of the repo — the raw→container resume path may have landed after our work — and find exactly which flow produced the name.

Here's the full picture — the name has two layers, and the `import-` prefix comes from the bundle-id generator in the import flow.

**How dashboard project names are derived.** The session list and chat header call `SessionRecord::project_name` (`src/hel_state.rs:552-571`), which tries in order:

1. managed worktree → directory name of the source repository
2. raw session → directory name of `project_directory`
3. bundle session → directory name of the configured bundle's primary repository `destination`
4. fallback when the bundle id isn't in config → the bundle id itself

Other surfaces — the new-session wizard's project picker and the wizard review's `Project:` row (`crates/hel-tui/src/lib.rs:5993`) — show the **bundle id** directly.

**Where the bundle id comes from.** Raw→container goes through the import machinery, and `resolve_bundle` (`src/hel_import.rs:2009-2095`) names the synthesized bundle: sanitized repo directory name (`setup_style_id`), then `unique_bundle_id` (`src/hel_import.rs:2157-2172`), which on a name collision produces `import-<name>`, then `import-<name>-2`, and so on. That's your `import-$projectname` — confirmed as the only source of that prefix in the codebase.

**Why it collided at all.** The prefix only appears when a bundle named `$projectname` already exists in your config but wasn't reused. Reuse requires an *exact* match (`bundle_matches`, `src/hel_import.rs:2097-2114`): same set of repository identities and the same primary as the session's detected git roots. Likely mismatch causes (can't confirm without your config): the existing bundle records the repo one way (`github:` owner/repo) while detection classified your checkout the other way (`local:` path, e.g. no or non-GitHub origin), you imported from a different clone path than the recorded `local:` one, or the session had edited files in a different set of git roots than the bundle lists.

One nuance: in the current code the session list would usually still display `$projectname` even for bundle `import-$projectname`, because arm 3 uses the repo *destination* (`hel`), not the bundle id. So you either hit the fallback (arm 4) or you're seeing the bundle id surface (picker/review) — either way the ugly part is that the id `import-$projectname` now lives permanently in your config and every surface that shows ids exposes it.

**Recommendation:** change `unique_bundle_id` to drop the `import-` prefix and disambiguate with numeric suffixes only — `hel`, `hel-2`, `hel-3`. That keeps the name recognizable and sorts next to its sibling. Separately, it's worth checking why your existing bundle wasn't reused — reuse is the better outcome than a second bundle, and if the cause is identity classification (github vs local), `bundle_matches` could be taught to treat them as equivalent when they point at the same repository. If you want, I'll make the `unique_bundle_id` change now and, if you paste the relevant bundle from your config, diagnose the reuse failure too.
